title: Sam Parr: Reddit growth hacks, collecting people, and building a decades-long business like Hampton
summary: Sam Parr tells how The Hustle got its first 100-150k subscribers through Reddit and Hacker News stunts, why he surrounds himself with more successful people, and why he now builds for decades with Hampton. He also covers cold outreach, media versus product businesses, and how to pick a next company.

principles.text: Be around people far more successful than you; the gap in ability is much smaller than the gap in results, which builds confidence.
principles.quote: they are not 10 times smarter than me some of them were but most are not but they're like 10 or 20 times more successful than I am

principles.text: Early audience growth: write stunt-style posts built to rank in specific subreddits, then convert the traffic with a strong pop-up.
principles.quote: I would write these blog posts that I thought would like go quote viral or rank high in a particular subreddit

principles.text: It's easier to build media around a product people love than to start with media and bolt a product on.
principles.quote: I think it's easier to have a product that people love and then to build media around it than it is to have media and then build a product around it

principles.text: Cold outreach works when it shows finished results, not ideas or offers to work for free.
principles.quote: it's far more interesting where it's like I've already done X Y and Z here's the website and here's the results

principles.text: Before a second company, research many industries methodically and interview founders, employees and customers before committing.
principles.quote: create like a notion dock of different categories of styles of companies and go and research them like crazy and go and interview the founders

principles.text: To build something that lasts, anchor on what customers will always want, as Amazon did, then innovate within that.
principles.quote: they're like what will customers always want they're always going to want cheap prices fast shipping and a large select selection of stuff so like let's just build our business on top of that
